title: Zero-Based Regulating
pass_4_primary_concern: The rule applies a blanket automatic-expiration structure across very different DOE programs without a part-specific explanation for why the one-year default is safe, workable, or the best fit.
pass_5_high_stakes_domain_reason: The proposal touches DOE contractor safety, nuclear-related programs, classified-information controls, waste and compensation regimes, and the continued force of regulations that affect public and worker protection.
pass_5_concise_why: The rule can let important DOE protections lapse before a rule-specific review is complete.
pass_5_most_important_consequence: A covered regulation may expire, or remain uncertain, before DOE finishes the review needed to decide whether it should continue.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: DOE relies on general housekeeping and broad executive-direction language to build a cross-cutting automatic-expiration regime, which is a different kind of authority claim than a part-specific amendment or repeal.
